Quick summary in the attached PDF (RDW_Commit_Proposal_Acme_20260309.pdf). TL;DR:
- Starter: 10M tokens/year — base price $0.00040/token with 5% effective discount delivered as credits
- Growth: 100M tokens/year — base price $0.00040/token with 15% discount
- Enterprise: 1B tokens/year — base price $0.00040/token with 30% discount + SLA credits and priority support

Notes/ask: please confirm which commit band looks closest to your procurement target and whether you need quarterly or annual billing. Ive also included a sample SOW for legal/procurement to start (SOW-Acme-Analytics.docx).

Thanks Rafael — useful start. A few clarifying questions before we loop procurement:
1) For Growth and Enterprise, are discounts applied as an up-front credit against committed spend or as a reduced per-token invoiced rate?
2) Do unused commit tokens roll forward to the next year or do they expire?
3) Is there a quarterly true-up (we pay for actual + true-up) or an annual true-up?
4) Any minimum monthly spend required for Enterprise?

Also, can you confirm whether quantization/opt-levels affect the discount tiers (we plan to use 8-bit models in prod and want to ensure pricing applies consistently). Marta and I will share expected monthly token volumes in a spreadsheet later today.

Appreciate the quick response — Jordan

Jordan — great questions, see answers below. Copying Marissa (pricing) and Stephanie (legal/enterprise ops) for transparency.

1) Discount mechanics: Growth & Enterprise are delivered as a reduced invoiced per-token rate (i.e., you are invoiced at the discounted rate up to the committed volume). For Starter we typically deliver an up-front credit applied against usage because the volumes are smaller and teams prefer a credit schedule.

2) Token rollover: we offer a 6-month limited rollover for any unused committed tokens (applies to Growth and Enterprise). Starter commits expire at the end of the 12-month term.

3) True-ups: we support either quarterly or annual true-ups. We recommend quarterly true-ups for predictable billing, but annual true-up is fine if procurement prefers it. True-up invoices are for overage at the discounted or base rate depending on the reconciliation model; final details will be in the SOW.

4) Enterprise minimums: Enterprise typically requires a 12-month minimum of 1B tokens or a negotiated equivalent in committed spend. Well include SLA credits (e.g., 5% credit for monthly uptime <99.5%) and priority queueing for inference capacity.

Quantization: pricing is model-architecture agnostic — the per-token pricing applies regardless of quantization. If you choose tooling that materially changes throughput/cost (custom runtimes or local private deployments), we can model custom economics under Redwood Private/Dedicated.

Attached: a revised one-page table with the three commit bands and examples (RDW_Commit_Proposal_Acme_20260309.pdf) and the SOW template.

Proposed next steps:
- Marta to confirm projected monthly tokens for the next 12 months (template attached)
- We prepare a PO-ready quote and DocuSign for the chosen tier
- Legal to redline SOW if needed

If youd like I can put together a short mutual action plan with milestones and target dates this week.

Best — Rafael

Commercial summary (Growth):
- Commit: 100,000,000 tokens/year (12-month term)
- Gross list price: $0.00040 per token -> $40,000 list for 100M tokens
- Discount: 15% off list applied as a reduced invoiced rate (effective price $0.00034/token) -> committed spend $34,000/year
- True-up cadence: quarterly true-up; overages billed at the Growth discounted rate
- Rollover: up to 6M unconsumed tokens can roll forward per quarter, up to a 6-month horizon
- SLA entitlements: 99.5% monthly uptime target, service credits per SOW for breaches
- Billing: monthly invoices with quarterly reconciliation; PO accepted
